# Pandamonium v1.0.44

Bash and web capabilities are now always-on with no owner-facing toggle. The adaptive intent router alone decides which tool schemas each request needs, and the chat send path no longer crashes on scope traps left by the adaptive refactor.

## MAD-882 — Agent: make bash/web tool toggles durable and server-side

### Problem

The chat input-bar bash/web toggles had been client-side only since the adaptive refactor removed the per-request tool flags. Leo toggled, the button lit up, the server never learned, and the agent still lacked the tool — an endless loop. Worse, the removed-toggle design left two latent send-path traps: a reference to a deleted `_isAgent` declaration that threw whenever the hidden web checkbox was checked, killing sends before the stream started, and a try-scoped `streamingTTS` that masked real stream errors with a second ReferenceError.

### Implementation

Per Leo's direction there is no owner-facing toggle at all. The remaining client-side remnants — the `/toggle bash|web` slash command entries and the dead localStorage persistence helpers — are removed; `/toggle` now manages research only. Bash and web stay enabled by default, and the adaptive intent router (`src/action_intents.py`) alone selects the tool schemas for each request. The send path now derives `_isAgent` from the selected agent target and declares `streamingTTS` outside the try block so the catch path stops TTS without masking the original error. Server-side capability policy (admin panel Tools, the agent's `manage_settings disable_tool/enable_tool`) is unchanged and remains the only off-switch.

### Product value and UI visibility

No toggle buttons exist in the chat UI — web search and shell are simply available when the agent determines the request needs them. Sends complete reliably even with stale toggle state present, and stream failures surface the real error instead of a confusing scope error. Users who deliberately disabled a capability through the admin panel or the agent's settings tools can still re-enable it the same way.

### Verification

Source guards pin the always-on contract: no bash/web toggle buttons in the UI, `/toggle` limited to research, no client-side tool-toggle persistence, and both repaired declarations in `static/js/chat.js`. The full Python suite passes (5,598 passed, 5 skipped) and the full browser suite passes (96/96), including the chat-turn-disclosure, workspace, and New Chat specs that previously failed on the trap. Required CI gates publication, and the signed artifact is verified against the exact tag.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

Bash and web are enabled by default; no configuration is required. An explicit server-side disable (admin panel Tools or `manage_settings disable_tool`) still removes them until re-enabled there — that is the deliberate policy layer, not a chat toggle. The deep-research pipeline does not read `disabled_tools` and is unaffected. If an existing installation has stale bash/web entries in `settings.json → disabled_tools`, clear them once via the admin panel or `manage_settings enable_tool shell` / `enable_tool search`. Installation remains operator-owned; MAD-882 closes on publication with live verification by the operator.

## MAD-802 — Agent: finalize adaptive tools, natural approvals, and voice responses

### Problem

The MAD-802 adaptive-routing refactor removed the per-request tool flags and the old chat/agent mode declaration, but two references survived in the send path: `_isAgent` and a try-scoped `streamingTTS`. Any stream error, or any send with the hidden web checkbox checked, threw a scope ReferenceError that either killed the turn before the stream or masked the real failure.

### Implementation

This release completes that residual: `_isAgent` is derived from the selected agent target and `streamingTTS` is declared outside the try block, restoring the agent-turn loading/timeout branches and an error path that reports the actual failure. No modes were reintroduced and no routing behavior changed.

### Product value and UI visibility

Agent sends behave identically to before, except they no longer crash on stale toggle state and stream errors surface honestly instead of as a confusing scope error. There is no visible UI change.

### Verification

Source guards pin both declarations in `static/js/chat.js`. The full Python suite (5,598 passed, 5 skipped) and full browser suite (96/96) pass, including the disclosure, workspace, and New Chat specs that previously reproduced the crash.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

No configuration changes. MAD-802's broader acceptance remains tracked in its own Linear issue; this release covers only the residual send-path repair it left behind.
